On TarUtilsTest::testName (a NUL-free 'abcdefghij' field at offset 1 of a 20-byte buffer) its scan, bounded only by NUL, appends past the field and throws AIOOBE at index 20. That breaks its promise to append the characters of the entry name into 'the buffer created for the entry name' (hop 3 documents that buffer's capacity as the field length; hop 4 calls it 'the buffer created for that field'). Each hop does exactly what its javadoc says it does itself: hops 1, 2 and 4 pass the arguments on unchanged, and hop 3 creates StringBuffer(length), delegates and returns the String. All four hops say the buffer 'is passed on without being copied', which rules out handing the gold a NUL-terminated copy, and none says more than its code does. (c) No competing repair. The only edits that pass the trigger, the ownership tests and the full suite are of four kinds: a terminated copy made in hop 3 or hop 4, which contradicts those hops' 'without being copied' javadoc; a catch-and-truncate in hop 3, a two-line bypass that cuts the gold's output after it throws; and a terminated copy made in the facade, a caller-side pre-filter. So it is not consistent with every hop's documentation, and I record it as a bypass.
